question_text: Explain how a browser uses a server’s digital certificate when establishing an HTTPS connection to a named website.
adaptation_rationale: Correct certificate direction and role; do not reproduce erroneous simplified handshake. Scenario and wording rewritten; source reasoning retained only within supported 2027 scope.
solution: Certificate binds the server’s identity/domain to a public key. Browser checks trusted issuer/signature and validity/domain match. Successful checks help authenticate the intended server and support secure connection establishment; this does not itself authenticate the human visitor.

marking_points.criterion: Certificate binds identity/domain and public key.
Checks trusted issuer/signature and validity/domain match.
Links checks to authenticating intended server, not the browser user.
